meta.title: Adoption Design
meta.sub: You leave this session with: Chapter 6 — who adopts first, what actually blocks them, and what you'd do about it

moves.detail: Read Ch. 6. Note that its real barrier is not the one vendors said out loud.
Name your adopters. Real roles, real people — not ‘the community’.
Separate what people SAY blocks them from what actually does.
One move per segment. Structural, not motivational.
Partner tests whether your ‘real barrier’ is just the stated one reworded.

model.label: THE MODEL — how the Carmen Market study did it
model.html:
✎ THE SPINE OF THE WHOLE COURSE. Everything up to now was diagnosis. This is the chapter the entire course has been aiming at, because it is where the thesis gets tested: innovation = invention + adoption. You already know the technology works. This is where you prove you know whether anyone will use it.

Stated barriers: fees and signal reliability. Real barrier: fear that a digital transaction record becomes a tax record.

And then the move that makes it a real chapter: “This study does not propose to solve that fear with a feature; it proposes to solve it with an explicit written assurance from the treasurer's office, secured before the pilot begins.”

Notice they did not target the laggards at all. Ten stalls, early adopters only, cash kept permanently for everyone else.

steps.label: STEP 1 — Your adopter segments
steps.instruction: Name roles you could actually walk up to and talk to. If you write ‘the youth’ or ‘the community’, you have not done this step.

columns.name: What you would do about them

steps.label: STEP 2 — Stated barrier
steps.instruction: These are almost never the same thing as the real barrier. The gap between them is where your chapter earns its marks.

steps.label: STEP 2 (cont.) — Real barrier
steps.instruction: Point to the evidence, not just a hunch.
steps.prefix: What we think ACTUALLY blocks them — and what evidence points there:

steps.label: STEP 3 — The move
steps.instruction: Structural, not motivational. ‘We will raise awareness’ is not a move. ‘We will get X in writing from Y before Z happens’ is.
steps.prefix: To address the real barrier, someone specific must do something specific before the pilot begins. Who, what, and when:

trap.label: THE TRAP
trap.html: Two traps. First: your ‘real barrier’ turns out to be the stated barrier in different words — ‘they said fees, and the real problem is… the cost.’ That is not analysis. Second, and worse: solving a structural barrier with a motivational fix. If people do not trust the system, a seminar will not fix it, a poster will not fix it, and an awareness campaign will not fix it. LAAG Bohol did not fail from insufficient enthusiasm.

peer_check.label: PEER CHECK
peer_check.instruction: Swap with another team. Their job is not to be nice — it is to find the specific weakness named below.
peer_check.task: Read their stated barrier, then their real barrier. Are they genuinely different, or the same thing reworded? Then read their move: is it structural, or is it ‘we will encourage people’? Write your verdict plainly.

file_it.label: FILE IT
file_it.instruction: Date it, initial it, and add it to your team's dossier folder. A chapter that is not filed does not exist.
